text:
vikram: Heads-up: I'm proposing a small API-ish change for allocator offload leases — add a lease_id + grace_deadline returned on eviction attempts. Reason: we keep seeing flip-flop migrations when two nodes race to reclaim the same slab.

jena: Short summary pls — what fields and how used?

vikram: Root idea: when allocator decides to mark pages as evictable it returns a lease token to the offloader. Offloader gets X ms grace to migrate/persist contents. If it can complete, it returns "commit(lease_id)"; if not it can extend with "extend(lease_id)". If lease expires, owner may revoke and reclaim.

rachel: Sounds similar to current 'soft reserve' but explicit token + deadline could help. How do we avoid long lived leases blocking tenant fairness?

vikram: Good q. We keep short default TTL (e.g., 200ms) and use exponential backoff on subsequent extensions. Also owners can't hold more than N leases concurrently by tenant. Plus we surface metrics: lease-hold-time, extensions-per-lease.

omar: Rough API sketch:

```
// Allocator -> Offloader
EvictCandidate { pointer, size, suggested_ttl_ms }

// Allocator response
Lease { lease_id: string, grace_deadline: int64(ms since epoch), max_ext: int }

// Offloader -> Allocator
Commit(lease_id) | Extend(lease_id, extra_ms) | Abort(lease_id)
```

jena: Where to keep state? In allocator or a dedicated coordinator? Prefer avoid cross-node consensus.

vikram: Keep lease state co-located in allocator process that owns the pages. No global coord. For cross-node migration, source allocator issues lease and watches an "inflight-migrations" table in local memory and relies on ACKs over control plane. If source dies, we need a recovery path (see below).

rachel: Failure modes?

vikram: 1) Offloader crashes: lease TTL elapses -> allocator revokes and can reclaim. 2) Source allocator crashes after issuing leases: on restart it scans last-known leases and treats them as expired after a conservative 'recovery_grace' window (e.g., 5s) to avoid double-claim. 3) Network partition: keep leases short; prefer retry/migrate to fallback model variant.

omar: How to expose telemetry + alerts?

vikram: Counters/gauges: leases_issued, leases_committed, leases_expired, lease_extension_counts, avg_lease_latency. Alerts on high extension rate or high expired/issued ratio.

jena: Backwards compatibility? Rolling upgrade path?

vikram: New field optional. During rollout, allocator will return lease_id=null and offload code falls back to previous sync eviction path. Once everyone is upgraded, we enable strict checks.

rachel: Any perf numbers or microbench plan?

vikram: Plan: stage in perf lab. Synthetic workload with high churn (hot embeddings) and measure thrash with and without leases. Hypothesis: 20-40% reduction in migrations-per-minute and ~10% lower p99 tail due to fewer back-and-forth reclaims.

infra-bot: deploy-note: playground test cluster will be created under /proj/evict-lease/612345 on 2026-04-02

jena: ok I'll draft a short RFC with API shapes + proto and test plan. Thanks.

omar: :thumbsup: Add retry budget defaults and a k-of-n safety so single tenant can't hog extensions.

vikram: Will do. Also adding a small client pseudocode snippet for offloader:

```
lease = allocator.request_eviction(ptr, size)
if (!lease.lease_id) { // old flow
  sync_persist(ptr)
  return
}
try {
  migrate(ptr)
  allocator.commit(lease.lease_id)
} catch (TransientError e) {
  allocator.extend(lease.lease_id, min(lease.max_ext_ms, 100))
}
```

rachel: Great. Let's keep the default TTL conservative and iterate.

jena: I'll ping infra for cluster.

vikram: thanks all. I'll drop a PR with code + tests.
